subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in configurable permission policy for agent-created user-facing files, and which write paths and default modes are allowed to participate?
rationale: The request adds config surface and changes local filesystem access semantics across security-sensitive tool paths, so automation should not choose the permanent user-output versus private-state boundary.

options.title: Approve scoped user-output policy
options.body: Add an opt-in policy for user-facing outputs while explicitly excluding config, credentials, auth, session, memory, and private state paths.

options.title: Use fixed per-path defaults
options.body: Fix only selected user-output paths such as managed media or sandbox-created artifacts without adding a general config knob.

options.title: Document external permission management
options.body: Keep OpenClaw defaults unchanged and document host ACL, user, group, umask, or container setup as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped user-output policy
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in policy for user-facing outputs while explicitly excluding config, credentials, auth, session, memory, and private state paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent filesystem guard and sandbox mutation history is the strongest available signal for deciding the safe permission boundary.
